To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vinca-domain ligand binding induces a large-scale polymorphism in protofilament-like tubulin assemblies that can be explained on the basis of local differences in their binding to tubulin.
the vinca-domain ligand ustiloxin binds to tubulin at the inter-heterodimetric interface of the heterodimer and stabilizes a protofilament-like assembly of tubulin, giving rise to rings and helices.

(i) the vinca domain binds to a site on tubulin that includes the inter-heterodimetric interface and the C-terminal tail of β-tubulin and (ii) the vinca-domain ligand ustiloxin binds to this site with high affinity, and the resulting complex can be used to study the structural plasticity of tubulins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of microtubules assembly and the design of new antimitotic agents.
tubulin assembly and with the structural and functional basis of its inhibition by vinca domain ligands.
the structural plasticity of tubulins in the presence of vinca-domain ligand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vinca-domain ligand binding to tubulin is a highly plastic process.
the vinca-domain ligand-binding pocket is not a rigid cavity, and that it can adapt its shape to accommodate a variety of ligands.

vinca-domain ligand-induced structural plasticity of tubulins is not only a matter of tubulin conformation, as suggested previously, but also a matter of the local interactions between tubulin and the ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of ustilxoin D bound to the tubulin complex T(2)R provides a detailed view of the interactions of a vinca domain ligand with tubulin and a rationale for the polymorphism of protofilament-like tubulin assemblies induced by vinca-domain binding.
vinca-domain ligand binding to tubulin induces structural plasticity in tubulin assembly, which can be modulated by subtle changes in the ligand's binding mode.

the structural plasticity of tubulins and the structural plasticity in the tubulin-ustiloxin interaction are both important for the formation of the protofilaments and the polymorphism of the assemblies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tubulin can tolerate a wide range of structural perturbations in the vinca domain binding pocket without affecting its overall assembly into microtubules.
the tubulin heterodimer is not a static entity, and that the binding of a ligand may induce conformational changes that can be transmitted to the rest of the microtubule lattice.
vinca-domain ligand binding induces a local structural change in the inter-heterodimetric interface of the tubulin heterodimer.
